---
title: "Flag Viewer"
format: html
resources:
  - w2560/*.png
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| cache: true
# List all PNG files and load country names from FlagCDN
flag_files <- list.files("w2560", pattern = "\\.png$")
country_names <- jsonlite::read_json("https://flagcdn.com/en/codes.json")

# Sample a 16x10 grid of RGB values from each flag to capture color and layout
features <- t(sapply(file.path("w2560", flag_files), \(f) {
  img <- png::readPNG(f)
  d <- dim(img)
  rows <- round(seq(1, d[1], length.out = 10))
  cols <- round(seq(1, d[2], length.out = 16))
  if (length(d) == 2) {
    sub <- img[rows, cols]
    c(sub, sub, sub)
  } else {
    c(img[rows, cols, 1], img[rows, cols, 2], img[rows, cols, 3])
  }
}))

# Find the closest non-identical flag for each country using Euclidean distance
dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist(features))
dist_mat[dist_mat < 0.01] <- Inf
similar_flags <- setNames(
  as.list(flag_files[apply(dist_mat, 1, which.min)]),
  flag_files
)
```

```{r}
# Exclude self-matches and territories that fly a parent country's identical flag
codes <- sub("\\.png$", "", flag_files)
duplicate_territories <- c("um", "hm", "bv", "sj", "bq", "gf", "gp", "mf", "pm", "re", "wf", "yt", "bl", "gb-nir", "sh")
same_flag_mask <- is.infinite(dist_mat)
same_flag_mask[, codes %in% duplicate_territories] <- TRUE
diag(same_flag_mask) <- TRUE

# Group flags by historical design families and match within family
families <- list(
  nordic = c("dk", "se", "no", "fi", "is", "fo", "ax"),
  british = c("gb", "au", "nz", "fj", "tv", "vg", "ky", "bm", "fk", "gs", "io", "ms", "pn", "sh", "tc", "ai", "ck", "nu", "us", "lr", "my"),
  panslavic = c("ru", "rs", "si", "sk", "cz", "hr", "bg", "nl", "lu"),
  panarab = c("eg", "iq", "sy", "ye", "sd", "jo", "ps", "kw", "ae", "eh", "ly"),
  panafrican = c("et", "gh", "sn", "ml", "gn", "cm", "cg", "bj", "tg", "bf", "gw", "st", "zm", "zw", "mw", "ke", "ss", "za", "jm", "gd", "kn", "gy"),
  tricolor = c("fr", "it", "ie", "be", "ro", "td", "md", "ad", "mx", "pe", "ci"),
  bolivarian_ca = c("co", "ec", "ve", "gt", "hn", "sv", "ni", "cr", "ar", "uy"),
  crescent = c("tr", "tn", "dz", "mr", "pk", "az", "uz", "tm", "sg", "mv", "km"),
  iberian_stars = c("es", "pt", "cu", "pr", "ph", "cl", "pa")
)
family_descriptions <- list(
  nordic = "Both flags belong to the Nordic Cross tradition, which originated with Denmark's 13th-century Dannebrog. Neighboring Scandinavian and Nordic nations adopted the off-center cross to reflect shared heritage.",
  british = "Both flags trace their design to British maritime ensigns and colonial cantons (or the East India Company stripes that inspired the U.S., Liberian, and Malaysian flags).",
  panslavic = "These flags draw from the 17th-century Dutch-inspired Russian tricolor and the 1848 Pan-Slavic Congress in Prague, which adopted red, white, and blue as colors of solidarity.",
  panarab = "Both flags share the Pan-Arab colors (red, white, black, and green) deriving from the 1916 Arab Revolt flag and the 1952 Arab Liberation tricolor.",
  panafrican = "These flags use the Pan-African colors inspired by Ethiopia's historic tricolor—the oldest independent African nation—adopted across Africa and the Caribbean during independence movements.",
  tricolor = "Both flags follow the vertical tricolor model popularized by the 1794 French Revolutionary flag, where three equal vertical bands symbolized republican liberty and nationhood.",
  bolivarian_ca = "These flags trace back to Early 19th-century South and Central American independence movements—either Francisco de Miranda's Gran Colombia tricolor or the blue-white-blue stripes of the United Provinces.",
  crescent = "Both flags feature the crescent and star motif popularized across the Islamic world through centuries of Ottoman and regional vexillological tradition.",
  iberian_stars = "These flags share historical roots in Iberian heraldry or the 19th-century independence banners of Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines, and Chile."
)
hist_dist <- dist_mat
history_notes <- setNames(
  as.list(rep("These two flags share closely aligned vexillological proportions, color symbolism, and regional design traditions.", length(flag_files))),
  flag_files
)
for (fam_name in names(families)) {
  fam <- families[[fam_name]]
  idx <- which(codes %in% fam)
  hist_dist[idx, idx] <- hist_dist[idx, idx] * 0.2
  for (f in flag_files[idx]) {
    history_notes[[f]] <- family_descriptions[[fam_name]]
  }
}
hist_dist[same_flag_mask] <- Inf
similar_history <- setNames(as.list(flag_files[apply(hist_dist, 1, which.min)]), flag_files)

ojs_define(
  flag_files = flag_files,
  country_names = country_names,
  similar_history = similar_history,
  history_notes = history_notes
)
```

```{ojs}
// 1. User selects a flag
viewof selected_flag = Inputs.select(flag_files, {
  label: "Select a flag:",
  value: "us.png"
})

selected_country = country_names[selected_flag.replace(".png", "")]

html`
  <div>
    <h3>Selected Flag</h3>
    <img src="w2560/${selected_flag}" style="max-width: 400px; border: 1px solid #ccc;">
    <p style="font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5rem;">${selected_country}</p>
  </div>
`
```

```{ojs}
// 2. Automatically look up and display the most similar flag based on history of design
similar_flag = similar_history[selected_flag]
similar_country = country_names[similar_flag.replace(".png", "")]
history_text = history_notes[selected_flag]

html`
  <div>
    <h3>Most Similar Flag (History of Design)</h3>
    <img src="w2560/${similar_flag}" style="max-width: 400px; border: 1px solid #ccc;">
    <p style="font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5rem;">${similar_country} (${similar_flag})</p>
    <p style="max-width: 500px; color: #444;">${history_text}</p>
  </div>
`
```
